artworks.title: Diana of Versailles
artworks.description: A marble statue of the huntress goddess striding beside a small deer, reaching over her shoulder toward her quiver — a Roman copy associated with a Greek original attributed to Leochares. Long a fixture of the French royal collections, it is displayed at the Louvre, Paris.

artworks.title: Diana and Actaeon
artworks.description: An oil painting of the fatal moment when the hunter Actaeon stumbles upon Diana and her nymphs bathing at a spring, the goddess's outraged glance already sealing his doom. One of Titian's celebrated poesie painted for Philip II of Spain, it is jointly owned by the National Gallery, London, and the National Galleries of Scotland.

artworks.title: The Lady of Ephesus
artworks.description: A marble cult statue of Artemis in her distinctive Ephesian form, the torso covered with rows of oval protuberances and the tight skirt paneled with rows of animals. The image embodies the Anatolian mother-goddess aspect of Artemis worshipped at her great temple in Ephesus. It is preserved in the Ephesus Archaeological Museum.

films.title: Troy: Fall of a City
films.description: The BBC/Netflix cycle keeps Artemis in the shadow of Iphigenia's sacrifice — the huntress whose withheld winds demand a daughter's blood before the fleet can sail.

films.title: Blood of Zeus
films.description: Netflix's animated war of the gods keeps Artemis among the Olympian archers — the huntress as a combatant in a family conflict that spills from Olympus to earth.

films.title: Percy Jackson and the Olympians
films.description: Disney+'s adaptation brings Riordan's Hunt of Artemis toward the screen — the eternal maiden and her hunters as a living order inside a demigod coming-of-age saga.

films.title: Hercules: The Legendary Journeys
films.description: The syndicated Hercules cycle brings Artemis on-screen among the Olympians who meddle in mortal quests — the huntress as a 1990s television goddess with bow and veto.

popCulture.title: Hades
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Artemis' boons are crit and seek — the huntress as a clean shot from Olympus, cool-voiced and exact while Zagreus runs.

popCulture.title: Hades II
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: She remains among the Olympian hunters in the sequel, still the goddess of the clean kill as Melinoë takes the field.

popCulture.title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians
popCulture.creator: Rick Riordan
popCulture.description: Riordan's Titan's Curse arc makes Artemis's Hunt a refuge and a battlefield — the eternal maiden who takes demigod girls into a sisterhood that never ages.

popCulture.title: Assassin's Creed Odyssey
popCulture.creator: Ubisoft Quebec
popCulture.description: The open-world Peloponnese is dotted with Artemis shrines and the goddess's sacred animals — the huntress as the wild edge of a Classical Greece you can climb.

popCulture.title: Lore Olympus
popCulture.creator: Rachel Smythe
popCulture.description: Smythe's Webtoon draws Artemis as Apollo's twin with bow and boundaries — the huntress holding the line while Olympus's softer scandals unfold.

music.title: La Calisto
music.description: Cavalli's Venetian comedy centres Diana's nymph Calisto and the goddess's own chastity code — Artemis as the moonlit law the plot keeps breaking.

music.title: Iphigénie en Aulide
music.description: Gluck's reform tragedy opens on Diana's withheld winds: the huntress who will not let the Greek fleet sail for Troy until Agamemnon pays with his daughter.

music.title: Actéon
music.description: Charpentier's miniature tragédie en musique stages the bath of Diane: the hunter Actéon sees what he should not, and the goddess turns him into the stag his own hounds tear apart.

music.title: Hippolyte et Aricie
music.description: Rameau's first tragédie en musique gives Diane the opera's protective hand over Hippolytus — the huntress as guardian of chastity against Phèdre's and Neptune's storms.
